subject: chemistry
title: Solids, liquids and gases — what are particles doing?

scenes.narration: Everything around you is made of tiny particles. In a solid, like ice, the particles are packed tightly and can only wiggle in place. That's why a solid keeps its shape.
Now let's heat it. The particles get energy, move faster and start sliding past each other. The ice melts into water — a liquid. A liquid flows and takes the shape of its container.
Heat it even more and the particles zoom around freely, far apart from each other. The water boils and becomes steam — a gas. A gas spreads out to fill any space.
Cool the steam down and the particles slow down and come closer again. Steam turns back into water drops. This is called condensation — like water drops on a cold glass!

questions.prompt: In which state are the particles farthest apart?
questions.explanation: Gas particles move freely and spread far apart — that's why gases fill any space.
